explain.say: Here is a secret that great readers know: they read things more than once! Reading again is not cheating. It is a smart reading tool. Look at the steps on the board.

faq.q: How do I know if it makes sense?
faq.a: Ask yourself: could this really happen? Does it sound like real talking? If it sounds odd, read it again.
asks: How do I check a sentence?

faq.q: Why should I read it again?
faq.a: The second time, your brain already knows some words, so it can think about the meaning. Things often become clear on the second read.

faq.q: What does in your own words mean?
faq.a: It means telling what you read using your own way of talking, not reading it out again. Like telling a friend what happened.
asks: How do I say it my way?

faq.a: Not at all! Good readers often go back and read again. It is one of the best ways to understand.

faq.q: What if it still does not make sense?
faq.a: Look at the pictures, read the sentence before it, or ask a teacher or grown-up. Asking for help is a smart reader move too.

facts: Reading the same text more than once is called repeated reading, and teachers often use it to build smooth, confident reading.
Stopping to check whether a sentence makes sense is a habit of strong readers.

quiz.show: A sentence does not make sense. What now?
quiz.why: Reading it again often makes the meaning clear.
